findings.name: Ordinary application SQL could bypass intended child sign-in
findings.historicalBoundary: guardian_finish was executable by ritc_app and did not require guardian_child_signin; guardian_admit_signin accepted a caller-supplied copy of guardian_enrollment.child_email_digest after only checking that the supplied subject had some confirmed email.
reproduction: Seed a valid guardian, live guardian device/session, reviewed enrollment, and one trusted fixture provider event.
As ritc_test_runtime, advance enrollment through the permitted consent/claim/approval states and INSERT a claim for a different confirmed nonadult subject/session.
With zero guardian_child_signin rows, invoke SELECT ritc.guardian_finish(h,claim,issuer,subject,session,pairing_hash,old_attempt_email_digest,new_device_id,device_hash).
Roll back to the pre-finalization savepoint, then invoke SELECT ritc.guardian_admit_signin(h,invite,issuer,wrong_subject,wrong_session,copied_setup_child_email_digest).
findings.fix: Admission/finalization moved behind the separate verifier connection. Application EXECUTE was revoked from the original and new functions; trusted finalization checks the exact admitted subject/session and current confirmed emails.
findings.currentExpected: All original/new application-role calls reject with SQLSTATE 42501

findings.name: Trusted finalization could race a pending child's zero-target erasure
findings.historicalBoundary: The initial application preparation released its shared identity fence before the separate trusted finalization transaction. The trusted function checked identity_blocked before waiting for the household lock but did not hold the shared identity advisory fence.
reproduction: Seed a pending approved claim with an admitted child subject/session and no child member yet.
Hold the household row lock in a third connection.
Start guardian_finish_verified on the verifier connection and wait until it blocks on the household row.

Start privacy_request for the still-pending child on the application connection. It obtains the exclusive identity fence, sees no member, creates a zero-target job, and waits on the household inside the identity_erasure trigger.
Release the household lock; finalization commits first, then erasure accepts and deletes the enrollment.
findings.expected: An accepted pending-identity deletion must not leave a newly created untargeted child profile.
findings.fix: Both trusted admission and finalization now acquire the same nonblocking shared identity advisory fences for child and initiating guardian before acquiring the household lock, then recheck current authority.

currentExpected.finalization_first: Finalization commits; deletion rejects adult_scope_required instead of falsely accepting an empty target set.
currentExpected.deletion_first: Deletion accepts; finalization rejects; no child member remains.

acceptanceLimits: This is source and disposable PostgreSQL/HTTP evidence, not evidence of a successful live KWS delivery/adult verification or production configuration.
Operator-approved notices, retention, provider credentials, signing/billing/deployment prerequisites and intended-device acceptance remain separate release requirements.
No remaining authority blocker was found in the current boundaries exercised by this independent review.
